events.title: James II Becomes King of England
events.description: On the death of his brother Charles II, James II of England, who was also James VII of Scotland, took the throne. He was a Catholic monarch ruling a largely Protestant kingdom.
events.significance: His reign ended in the Glorious Revolution of 1688. That upheaval strengthened Parliament and shaped modern constitutional monarchy in Britain.

events.title: France and the United States Sign Treaties of Alliance
events.description: In Paris, American and French representatives signed a Treaty of Alliance and a Treaty of Amity and Commerce. With them France formally recognized the young United States.
events.significance: French money, troops and naval power became vital to the American Revolutionary War, and they helped bring about the victory at Yorktown.

events.title: Treaty of Waitangi Is Signed
events.description: Representatives of the British Crown and many Māori chiefs signed the Treaty of Waitangi at Waitangi in the Bay of Islands. It became the founding document of modern New Zealand.
events.significance: Differences between the English and Māori versions of the text have driven debate, legal claims and efforts at reconciliation ever since. The treaty remains central to New Zealand's national identity.

events.title: Poland's Round Table Talks Begin
events.description: The Polish government opened negotiations with the opposition, including the Solidarity movement, in Warsaw. The talks led to an agreement on partially free elections.
events.significance: The talks became a model for peaceful transitions. They helped set off the wave of changes that ended communist rule across Eastern Europe in 1989.
